about.title: Monte Sereno Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Monte Sereno is a small, quiet city tucked into Santa Clara County, but its roads still see real crashes — public records show 6 injury collisions and 7 injured people in 2024 alone. Local corridors like Saratoga Los Gatos Road, Rt 9, La Rinconada Drive, and Winchester Boulevard see the bulk of reported collisions, with Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up often in the data. Whether you were rear-ended near a stop sign or hit while crossing an intersection, the aftermath can feel disorienting — medical visits, missed work, an insurance adjuster calling before you've caught your breath. We're a personal injury law team ready to review your situation, explain your options, and help you understand what preserving evidence early might mean for your claim. There's no obligation, and no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a road maintained by the county — was involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for the crash, you may still recover a percentage of damages. We can help make sure your share of fault isn't overstated by the other driver's insurer.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, But Insurers Push Back Anyway
items.desc: California doesn't cap pain-and-suffering damages in most car accident cases, yet insurance companies still try to minimize them early — often through a recorded statement. It's worth speaking with us before you say anything on the record.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use early statements, made while you're still shaken or unsure of your injuries, to minimize what they eventually pay. We can advise you on what to say and what to hold off on.

items.question: Monte Sereno is a small city — does that affect my claim?
items.answer: Not directly. Even with only a handful of reported injury collisions each year, the same California laws on fault, deadlines, and damages apply whether the crash happened on La Rinconada Drive or a busier freeway. What matters is the evidence from your specific crash, not the size of the city.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
